subject: history_social
passage: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, opened in 1881, climbs almost 2,000 meters from the plains of West Bengal to the hill town of Darjeeling on tracks only 61 centimeters ______ to gain height on slopes too steep to climb directly, its engineers built loops and zigzags into the line. The small trains, affectionately called toy trains, still run today.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway … climbs almost 2,000 meters … on tracks only 61 centimeters apart" is a complete sentence. "To gain height on slopes too steep to climb directly, its engineers built loops and zigzags into the line" is a second complete sentence. Two closely related independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Which" would turn the second clause into a description of the tracks, but "which to gain height … its engineers built loops" has no place for "which" in the clause and makes no grammatical sense.
explanation.B: Correct. A semicolon correctly joins two closely related independent clauses.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A comma alone can't join two independent clauses; this creates a comma splice.
explanation.D: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the two independent clauses run together (a run-on sentence).
